pages.summary: Colormaps for data: blue to yellow, perceptually uniform, and two rainbows.
body: A colormap is an n-by-3 matrix of RGB rows from 0 to 1 (64 rows unless n is given, or as many as the current figure's map has). `parula` (the default here) runs from blue through green to yellow; `viridis` from dark purple to yellow with lightness rising evenly, so that it reads correctly in gray and for most colour-blind readers; `turbo` is a rainbow whose lightness changes smoothly; `jet` the classic rainbow, whose bright band in the middle can suggest features that are not in the data.

examples.title: Four maps on one surface

pages.summary: The classic colormaps: grays, heat, and seasons.
body: `gray` runs from black to white; `bone` is gray with a tint of blue, `copper` black to light copper, `pink` pastel shades. `hot` goes black, red, yellow, white; `cool` cyan to magenta; and the seasons: `spring` magenta to yellow, `summer` green to yellow, `autumn` red to yellow, `winter` blue to green. Each takes the number of rows.

examples.title: Ten maps as bands
examples.code:
names = {'gray', 'bone', 'copper', 'pink', 'hot', 'cool', 'spring', 'summer', 'autumn', 'winter'};
for k = 1:10
    ax = subplot(10, 1, k);
    image(ax, 1:64), colormap(ax, feval(names{k}, 64)), axis off
    text(ax, -2, 1, names{k}, 'HorizontalAlignment', 'right')
end
gray(3)

pages.summary: Colormaps of distinct or repeating colours: the hues round the circle, the line colours, stripes, and a colour cube.
body: `hsv` runs through the hues of the colour circle, red back to red, which suits angles and phases. `lines` repeats the colours lines take in turn, `prism` six colours and `flag` red, white, blue and black over and over, for telling neighbouring levels apart; `white` is all white, and `colorcube` evenly spaced colours of a colour cube, then grays and pure tones.

examples.title: A phase in hues, and the line colours
examples.code:
[X, Y] = meshgrid(linspace(-1, 1, 101));
subplot(1, 2, 1), imagesc(angle(X + 1i*Y)), axis image off, colormap(gca, hsv(64)), title('hsv')
subplot(1, 2, 2), image(1:7), colormap(gca, lines(7)), axis off, title('lines')
flag(4)

pages.summary: A colormap brightened or darkened, drawn as its three columns, and turned round.
body: `brighten` raises each value of a colormap to a power, brighter for beta between 0 and 1, darker for beta between -1 and 0; given only beta it changes the current figure's map. `rgbplot` draws a map's red, green and blue columns against their row, in those colours, which shows how it was made. `spinmap` turns the current figure's map round for a few seconds, shifting its rows.

examples.title: Parula brighter, and how its columns run

pages.summary: Colours checked and given as RGB, and converted to and from hex codes.
body: `validatecolor` takes colours as names (`'red'`, `'r'`), hex codes (`'#FF8800'`, `'#F80'`) or RGB rows (doubles from 0 to 1, or integers scaled by their range) and gives them as rows of doubles, refusing anything that is not a colour; one colour unless `'multiple'`. `rgb2hex` writes RGB rows as `'#RRGGBB'` strings (`'#RGB'` with `'Shorthand', true` where it can), and `hex2rgb` reads them back.

examples.title: One colour three ways
examples.code:
validatecolor({'red', '#00FF80', 'b'}, 'multiple')
validatecolor(uint8([255 128 0]))
h = rgb2hex([1 0.5 0; 0 0 1])
rgb2hex([1 1 0], 'Shorthand', true)
hex2rgb(h)
